customer_jason: hey all — after last deploy our integration started failing when we request structured JSON (mode=json). parser throws 'Unexpected end of JSON input' intermittently. ~1 in 5 streams. :frowning:
customer_jason: small repro: we send prompt + this content and stream=true. sometimes the streamed chunks result in invalid JSON when concatenated by our client. example fragment we captured:
```json
{"invoice":"INV-2026-07","note":"LineA\\nLineB","path":"/data/orders/INV-2026-07"}
```
customer_jason: the problem looks like either an extra unescaped newline inside a quoted field or a chunk boundary splitting an escape sequence (we see things like "LineA\\nLi" then next chunk "neB").
support_josh: thanks @customer_jason — can you paste the exact curl you used? also which model + api version and region?
customer_jason: curl we used:
```bash
curl -sS -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rt-large","stream":true,"input":"generate invoice"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
customer_jason: model is redwood-rt-large, region: us-west-2, API key is long-lived. logs show 200 then client parser fails.
ingest-bot: New log entry: span=svc/generate id=span-7f2e level=error msg="parse_error: chunk-unescaped-delimiter"
eng_robin: digging in — likely two causes: (1) runtime streaming sometimes emits a chunk boundary in the middle of an escaped sequence (e.g. backslash + n split), (2) some clients reconstructing chunks incorrectly (need to concatenate raw bytes, not attempt UTF-8 decode per-chunk).
eng_robin: quick repro I ran locally reproduces "\\n" split when chunk size <= 16 bytes for that payload. can you confirm your client concatenates raw bytes and only UTF-8 decodes after full message?
customer_jason: our client does incremental decode per-data event (we use event-stream handler), hmm. we assumed each data: event is valid UTF-8.
support_josh: okay that's helpful. two things to try: (A) temporary workaround: set "stream":false to get atomic JSON responses until we fix streaming. (B) if you need streaming, change client to buffer raw bytes and only decode after reassembly. also upgrade SDK to 1.4.2 — it includes a streaming reassembly fix.
customer_jason: is streaming=false paid the same? worried about extra cost due to retries.
billing_sam: we can credit the extra retries while we investigate. ping me if you want immediate credits and we'll add a short-term usage adjustment.
customer_jason: thanks. can you confirm whether the runtime will be patched?
eng_robin: timeline: patch queued — will ensure chunker never splits an escape sequence by preferring split boundaries at UTF-8 codepoint boundaries and escape-safe offsets. deploy ETA: 24h for canary, 72h global. root cause: previously chunker used fixed byte windows without considering escaping context.
eng_robin: workaround for now: stream=false or client-side reassembly. sample client change (node):
```js
// don't do `utf8.decode(chunk)` per event, push raw Buffer then at end do Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8')
const chunks = [];
stream.on('data', (c) => chunks.push(c));
stream.on('end', () => {
  const body = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8');
  // parse body as JSON
});
```
support_josh: for immediate triage can you share one full failing capture (raw bytes) and the exact sdk version? we'll attach to the bug.
customer_jason: uploaded raw capture to the support ticket (link). SDK was 1.3.7. will try stream=false as a temporary fix.
support_josh: noted, we escalated to runtime team. I'll follow up when canary is up. :thumbsup:
billing_sam: credited 50 calls to your account id=acct_ABC123 for retry noise. you should see it in billing activity.
customer_jason: thanks everyone — appreciate the fast turnaround. will test the workaround and report back.
eng_robin: FYI we'll also add a regression test that injects escaped sequences at chunk boundaries to avoid regressions.
support_josh: closing loop: if you still see malformed payloads after SDK upgrade + client reassembly, re-open here and tag me.
